about: The format a Formula gives a General cell when it is entered (ADR-0047, second round). Microsoft does not document the rule for any function ExSheet declares (it does for DATE, TODAY and NOW, which ExSheet does not have), so the engine applies only what these cases have observed Excel to do: simple arithmetic (single-cell References, constants, + and -, parentheses) takes the format of the first formatted cell it reads, except that a date minus a date gives none; MIN and MAX over References take the format of their first formatted argument; anything else gives none. It applies only when the cell's format is General, and only when the Formula is entered. The uncertain cases record the engine's answer where Excel has not been asked.

cases.description: A date plus a number shows as a date
A number plus a date shows as a date: the first formatted Reference, not the first operand
A date minus a date is a number of days, and gives no format
A Formula that is one Reference takes that cell's format
A negated Reference in parentheses takes that cell's format
The first Reference whose cell is formatted gives the format, an unformatted one before it passed over
A cell formatted before the Formula is entered keeps its format
The format is taken once, at entry: formatting the cell read afterwards does not change it
A cell read in a formatted column gives the column's format
A Formula pasted as text takes a format as a typed one does
Multiplication over a date takes the date format (verification/2026-09-27-windows-excel-2, with real keys)
cases.oracleSkip: Through COM (Formula2 over a cell set by FormulaLocal) Excel gives this result no format, but typed with real keys it does (verification/2026-09-27-windows-excel-2); ask by keys
